controls.min: Almost no fixed conditions: learners choose format, grouping, starting point, and materials.
controls.max: Everything is fixed before learners arrive: roles, materials, format, and entry point are engineered.

controls.min: No meaningful friction; tasks are straightforward and information is complete.
controls.max: Contradictions, missing information, shifting goals, or time pressure make easy answers impossible.

controls.min: No meaningful learner choice; learners execute decisions made by the teacher or structure.
controls.max: Learner choices genuinely change what happens next for themselves and others.

controls.min: No defined success criteria; learners do not know what winning looks like.
controls.max: Explicit success criteria are understood upfront and require genuine thinking rather than recall.

designMoves.name: Create Constraint
designMoves.definition: Narrow the field so choices matter.

designMoves.name: Create Interdependence
designMoves.definition: Make learners rely on one another to move forward.

designMoves.name: Create Agency
designMoves.definition: Give learners choices that alter what happens next.

designMoves.name: Create Asymmetry
designMoves.definition: Distribute information, power, or resources unevenly.

designMoves.name: Create Urgency
designMoves.definition: Make timing part of the thinking problem.

designMoves.name: Create Uncertainty
designMoves.definition: Let learners act before the picture is complete.

designMoves.name: Create Opportunity
designMoves.definition: Open a consequential possibility learners can choose to pursue.

moves.title: The One-Sentence Rule
moves.example: Explain the system in one sentence before you may add detail.
moves.description: Use a tight form to reveal what learners believe is essential.

moves.title: Choose the Boundary
moves.example: Teams decide what is outside the scope—and defend the exclusion.
moves.description: Let learners define the edges of the problem.

moves.title: The Missing Piece
moves.example: Remove one familiar resource and ask students to redesign around its absence.
moves.description: Make the shape of the system visible through subtraction.

moves.title: Incomplete Brief
moves.example: Release only 70% of the evidence; learners list what they need and act anyway.
moves.description: Turn uncertainty into an explicit thinking condition.

moves.title: No Perfect Option
moves.example: Every available solution protects one value while compromising another.

moves.title: Midstream Dispatch
moves.example: Halfway through, a new source complicates the team’s strongest claim.
moves.description: Test whether thinking can adapt without collapsing.

moves.title: Learners Set the Rules
moves.example: Students draft three operating rules, then live with the consequences.
moves.description: Move authority from procedure-following to system-making.

moves.title: Role with Real Power
moves.example: Each stakeholder role controls one resource others must negotiate to access.
moves.description: Make perspective structural rather than theatrical.

moves.title: The Wild Card
moves.example: Each team earns one chance to rewrite a condition for everyone.
moves.description: Give learners bounded power to change the arena.

moves.title: Public Thinking Log
moves.example: Teams post each decision, evidence used, and what could change their mind.
moves.description: Score the quality and evolution of thinking, not only the outcome.

moves.title: Audience Questions Count
moves.example: A real audience scores which unanswered question the work makes urgent.
moves.description: Let reception shape the definition of success.

moves.title: Revision Is the Win
moves.example: The strongest score goes to the team that changes its thinking most intelligently.
moves.description: Reward responsiveness rather than stubborn certainty.

faders.label: Time
faders.downDescription: Spacious; as much time as needed

faders.label: Access
faders.downDescription: Fully restricted; only what learners know
faders.upDescription: Fully open; tools, AI, peers, and resources available

faders.label: Ambiguity
faders.upDescription: Deliberately open; learners must frame the problem

faders.label: Information Completeness
faders.upDescription: Significant information is missing or must be sought

faders.label: Stakes / Visibility
faders.upDescription: Public, consequential, and visible to a real audience

tensionRules.label: Pressure without power
tensionRules.message: High friction with little learner control can feel punitive. Raise EMPOWER or lower CHALLENGE.

tensionRules.label: Agency without anchor
tensionRules.message: Learners can change the arena, but success is hard to read. Clarify the SCOREBOARD.

tensionRules.label: Open terrain, high stakes
tensionRules.message: This can create powerful thinking if it is intentional. Make sure learners can read the purpose of the openness.

tensionRules.label: Everything balanced
tensionRules.message: Nothing is wrong—but no dial is doing distinctive design work yet. Is that intentional?
